title: Bitcoin mining difficulty drops 7.8% as miner exodus accelerates amid AI pivot

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: What does a 7.8% drop in Bitcoin mining difficulty say about the intersection of cryptocurrency and AI?

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Mining hardware is becoming obsolete as AI-driven mining farms optimize hash rates with machine learning and quantum-resistant algorithms.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: A miner exodus risks centralizing hash power, undermining decentralization and opening the door to state or corporate control over Bitcoin.

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Builders are deploying modular mining rigs and using renewable energy grids to make mining more efficient and less energy-intensive.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: If AI integrates seamlessly with blockchain, we could see a future where mining is automated, transparent, and powered by decentralized AI networks.

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: The future of Bitcoin may hinge on how well it adapts to AI, balancing innovation with the principles that made it revolutionary.

video_cue: A dynamic visualization of Bitcoin nodes shrinking as AI algorithms route hash power across a global network.
